SPRING SEASON APPROXIMATION FOR EARTHS RADIANCE AT THE MOON, AS DESCRIBED BY: 
 Glenar, Stubbs, Schwieterman, Robinson and Livengood, in:
 "Earthshine as an Illumination Source at the Moon"

Publication Status: Revised manuscript submitted to Icarus, Sept. 2018

SUMMARY:
------- 
A semiempirical approximation for Earths hemispherical average radiance, including uncertainties, as a  
function of wavelength, phase and sub-observer position (latitude and longitude), condensed from 
a two-month series of Virtual Planetary (VPL) models near spring equinox (March and April 2008).  
Wavelength coverage is 0.30 and 2.5 microns. This approximation is valid for sub-observer latitude 
between 30S and 30N (i.e. from a lunar perspective), and Earth orbital phase angles less than 60 degrees.
Earths diurnal average light curve is represented by a double Henyey-Greenstein phase function, and
diurnal brightness modulation is represented by the change in observable land fraction over a rotation.
Diurnal effects not explained by land fraction are attributed to cloud variability. To within the
uncertainties, this approximation is also valid for summer solstice, based on the examination of one 
additional VPL model series.  Other seasons have not been examined.
--------


I(g,CML,theta) =  Ibar00 * PHI(g,b) * { 1 + AL ( fLbar(theta) - fLbar_gmin ) } * { 1 + BL [ fL(CML,theta) - fLbar(theta) ] }

where: I(CML,g,theta) is hemispherical average radiance (W m-2 sr-1 micron-1) at a single wavelength
       g is Earth orbital phase angle (Sun-Earth-Observer angle)
       CML is the sub-observer central meridian west longitude (deg)
       theta is sub-observer latitude (deg)

       Ibar00 is the diurnally averaged radiance (W m-2 sr-1 micron-1) at g=0 deg, and theta=0 deg

       PHI(g,b) is Earths phase curve obtained from a symmetric, double Henyey-Greenstein phase function expression (PI(g,b))
         with b the wavelength dependent broadening coefficient. PHI(g,b) is normalized to a peak value of 1.0. 
         PHI(g,b) = (1/2) * ( PI(g,b) / PI(0,b) * ( 1 + cosg )   with,
         PI(g,b) =  (1/2) * (1-b^2) / (1- 2bcosg + b^2)^3/2   +   (1/2) * (1-b^2) / (1 + 2bcosg + b^2)^3/2 

       fL(CML,theta) is the fraction of the observed hemisphere occupied by land
         fL values are obtained by interpolation within a 37 X 11 array of fL values defined at
         CMLS OF 0,10,20 . . .360 DEG W, and latitudes of -20, -15,  . . 25, 30

       fLbar(theta) are diurnal-average values of fL (average of fL along the CML axis) 
         A quadratic approximation for fLbar is:  0.181  +  7.578 x 10^-4 * theta  +  1.1517 x 10^-5 * theta^2 

       fLbar_gmin is the value of fLbar at 0 phase angle:  fLbar_gmin ~ 0.190 

       AL is the wavelength dependent coefficient which accounts for changing land fraction
         (this alters the shape of the phase curve)

       BL is the wavelength dependent coefficient which defines the amplitude of the diurnal intensity modulation


Note:  Diurnal average light curves are obtained by omitting the last (diurnal) factor 
  
--------------------------------------
